main_body: Large hipped thatch roof (rows 5-50) over a log-plank wall front with a central doorway (rows 51-78) and a stone footing
top_band: Golden thatch roof slope from row 7 down to about row 50: light courses (#d8bb68 / #bc9a45) separated by dark course lines, with an outline at rows 5-6. It is a large lighter sloped surface above the darker log wall.
evidence: The roof reads as a big top slope with stepped hip edges widening toward the eaves, as in the Beodeul house references. A dark eave line and shaded strip at about rows 50-55 separate it from the vertical log wall. The doorway has an inset frame and a dark interior, and the entry gable bump projects forward. The wall is a front face below a clearly visible roof surface, so this is a valid 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5-6 lightness steps with per-course highlights and dark course lines. The log wall has varied browns, the medallions are shaded, the door has a stone-lined jamb, and the skull is a small detail. The outlines lean brown (6% neutral dark edge pixels). Flat-fill coverage is 2%, close to the references' 0%. Median colours per tile is 8, against 11 and 18 for the references. The 38 total colours is lower than both references (66 and 185), partly because of the locked palette and the repetitive thatch rows. Structure and craft are acceptable next to the references.
